sources: dengue_collection
https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/dengue-fever-guidance-data-and-analysis
UKHSA dengue guidance, data and analysis collection
dengue symptoms, diagnosis, travel association and epidemiology
The collection covers dengue symptoms, diagnosis and epidemiology.
It states that UK-reported cases are travel-associated because dengue does not occur locally in the UK.
dengue_green_book
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/dengue-the-green-book-chapter-15a
UKHSA dengue Green Book chapter
dengue immunisation information for public-health professionals
The publication provides dengue immunisation information for public-health professionals.
It directs users to the current National Travel Health Network and Centre chapter.
dengue_stats
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/dengue-laboratory-confirmed-cases-in-england-wales-and-northern-ireland
UKHSA laboratory-confirmed dengue statistics
provisional laboratory-confirmed dengue surveillance by month and travel history
The publication provides epidemiological data on laboratory-confirmed dengue cases.
Its data are organised by reporting period and country or region of travel.
zika_collection
https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/zika-virus-zikv-guidance
UKHSA Zika virus guidance collection
Zika symptoms, transmission, pregnancy, diagnosis and epidemiology
The collection brings together clinical, travel, pregnancy and laboratory guidance for Zika virus.
It identifies most UK cases as travel-associated.
zika_symptoms
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/zika-virus-symptoms-and-complications
UKHSA Zika symptoms and complications guidance
Zika clinical presentation, supportive treatment and uncommon complications
The guidance states that most infections are asymptomatic and symptomatic illness is usually mild and short-lived.
It identifies pregnancy-related congenital abnormalities and rare neurological complications as important concerns.
zika_transmission
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/zika-virus-transmission/zika-virus-transmission
UKHSA detailed Zika transmission guidance
mosquito, sexual, pregnancy and blood-transfusion routes of Zika transmission
The guidance identifies Aedes mosquito bites as the main transmission route.
It also covers sexual, pregnancy-associated and blood-transfusion transmission.
zika_sexual
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/zika-virus-preventing-infection-by-sexual-transmission
UKHSA Zika sexual-transmission prevention guidance
barrier methods and pregnancy-related precautions after possible Zika exposure
The guidance explains that sexual transmission can occur even when infection is asymptomatic.
It recommends consistent barrier methods for specified periods after possible exposure.
zika_testing
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/zika-virus-sample-testing-advice
UKHSA Zika sample-testing guidance
testing eligibility, sample types, laboratory methods and result interpretation
The guidance is for UK healthcare professionals arranging laboratory diagnosis of Zika virus infection.
It covers test eligibility, sample collection and interpretation of RIPL results.
zika_pregnancy_algorithm
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/zika-virus-interim-algorithm-for-assessing-pregnant-women-with-a-history-of-travel
UKHSA Zika pregnancy risk algorithm
assessment of pregnant women after travel to areas with Zika transmission risk
The flowchart supports assessment of pregnant women with possible travel-related Zika exposure.
The current algorithm was updated in April 2026.
